finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts::test titled 'always answers ok so yorkie does not retry' only exercises the trivial early-return path
evidence: Verified against the supplied sources: in `yorkie-event.controller.ts` the handler resolves `key = body.attributes?.key` → `undefined`, so `parsed` is `null` and it returns `{ ok: true }` at the `!parsed` guard — the spec case at `yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:66` posts exactly `{ type: 'DocumentRootChanged' }` with no `attributes`, so it never reaches `touchUpdatedAt`. The controller also has no try/catch around `await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(...)`, and no spec case makes the mock reject, so the claimed "always 200, never retry" property is indeed untested for the failure path; the test's title over-promises relative to what it exercises. Note the other specs do drive the `touchUpdatedAt` path (with a resolving mock), so coverage of the happy path exists — the genuine gap is only the rejection case. Impact is limited: a 500 on a DB outage causes Yorkie to retry, which is arguably the desired behaviour rather than a data-correctness bug, so this is a test-naming/coverage gap rather than a functional defect.
